'''''Begonia manicata''''' is a species of flowering plant in the family [[Begoniaceae]], native to Mexico and Central America.<ref name="105149-1" >{{cite web |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:105149-1 |title=''Begonia manicata'' Brongn. |author=<!--Not stated--> |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=Board of Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=24 July 2021 }}</ref>  It was collected from the [[Veracruz moist forests]] by [[Jean Jules Linden]], and later described in 1842.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Clark |first=Alice M. |date=March 1947 |title=B. Manicala, Brongn. Var. Aureo-Maculata |url=https://www.begonias.org/wp-content/uploads/_pda/2021/12/1947-March.pdf |journal=The Begonian |publisher=The American Begonia Society |volume=14 |issue=3 |pages=51-52}}</ref> The variety 'Aureo-maculata' has cream variegations in the foliage,<ref name="Sharp">{{cite book |last1=Sharp |first1=Peter G. |url=https://www.ibegonias.filemakerstudio.com.au/PeterSharp/DownToEarthWithBegonias.pdf |title=Down To Earth - With Begonias |date=2011 |pages=93 |access-date=3 February 2026}}</ref> and is called the leopard begonia.<ref>{{cite web |date=2021 |title=''Begonia manicata'' 'Aureo-maculata' leopard begonia |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/203455/Begonia-manicata-Aureo-maculata/Details |access-date=24 July 2021 |publisher=The Royal Horticultural Society}}</ref>

Though it is an upright [[Rhizomatous begonia|rhizomatous]] begonia, so the rhizome grows upwards instead of along the ground. When full-grown, the leaves can grow to 7 or more inches across. The flowers, which can be pink or white, appear in the winter. <ref name=":0" />

The specific epithet ''manicata'' means "cuff", and refers to the bands of red hairs at the end of each [[Petiole (botany)|petiole.]] In the varietal cognomen, ''aureo'' is from ''aureus'', which means "golden", and ''maculata'' means "spotted."<ref name=":0" />

''Begonia manicata'' has been used extensively in hybridization.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Schwerdtfeger |first=Louise |date=July 1947 |title=In Hybridizing |url=https://www.begonias.org/wp-content/uploads/_pda/2021/12/1947-July.pdf |journal=The Begonian |publisher=The American Begonia Society |volume=14 |issue=7 |pages=125}}</ref> In particular, it is the male parent of the cultivar B. 'Erythrophylla', (the beefsteak begonia) and the female parent of the cultivar B. 'Verschaffeltii.'<ref name=":0" />
